chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Overseas tours with Ella and Sarah; Hamburg and Manchester encores
summary: Dating his European trips with Ella to about 1963-65 and with Sarah to the mid-1950s, plus the Hamburg and Manchester ovations.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You mentioned Ella getting standing ovations in Hamburg. Do you remember what year that was, because it helps to sort of put these things in perspective if we can remember the years.
All right, I joined Ella -- oh, boy, let me -- this is '78, right?
Uh-huh.

In sixty -- about '65 -- '64 or '65, somewhere right around there. A little earlier. No, no, a little earlier. In -- I think that's when I first went to Europe with her, when she was getting those standing ovations.
Uh-huh. Okay. Now.

Speaking about Ella's standing ovations, this was in Hamburg, Germany, and Norman Granz, her manager, had chartered a plane, and we could fly any time we wanted to fly, you know? We'd finished this concert and had gone back to our dressing rooms to change, to get on the plane, to change our clothes. And the audience came around the stage and surrounded the stage, and we had to come out and perform again. And I had a sweater on. At first I'd had a tuxedo. You know how you dress up to perform a show. And so we did it all over again. They just wouldn't leave. And another time we had this to happen was in Manchester, England, and they wouldn't leave, the audience wouldn't leave, you know, so Ellington just started playing, 'God Bless the Queen.'
(Laughter)
So everybody started walking out after that. Because we weren't about to get out of town that night, you know.
Did you ever have that experience with audiences in the United States?
Yes, I think so.
Do you remember when? Or with whom?

Yeah, well -- yeah, I think with Sarah, Sarah Vaughan, and with Ella, but I just don't remember when. But I've had experiences like that here in the States. It's just that I just don't remember when it was, you know? Because Sarah and I travelled so much, you know. We covered a lot of years and a lot of towns and everything, you know.
You said that time in Hamburg was in -- in '63, was the first time you went overseas with Ella. How many times did you go overseas with Ella?
Oh, about three times.
When were the other times?

Every year. I was with her about three or four years. Every year we'd go, in the first of the year, around January and February, we would go overseas. And we always had a great reception, you know, always had a great reception. When I was over there with Sarah we had a great reception. I think I first went there with Sarah in the middle '50s, you know. Like I had gotten to the point where I began to know London and Paris so well, I knew how to get on the Metro, you know the subway --
Uh-huh.
-- and go where I wanted to go. And the
subway in London.
When you were touring with Sarah, who else was in your group? Was it a trio, or --
No, I was really the solo accompanist.
Oh.

And we'd just pick up whomever the band had. At that point, I think they had Illinois Jacquet's band, and I think it was Joe Jones, who was the famous drummer with Basie, and I think Al Lucas was the bass player. So we were never in trouble.
No.
(Laughter)
We always had good music with us, you know.
